5: # L1 — часть 01 (PDF с. 1–3)
6: 
7: [порождено] Обзор и синтез. TiN предлагается как плазмонная альтернатива Au: у Au 5–50 нм пик 520–540 нм, вне окна прозрачности 670–1000 нм (с. 1). Аннотация: пик TiN 640–700 нм и хвост >800 нм даже при <7 нм; in vitro на клеточных моделях — низкая цитотоксичность и захват; фотоТТ на культуре U87–MG в ближнем ИК (с. 1–2). Это клеточные опыты, не лечение людей. Абляция: Yb:KGW 1025 нм, 1–100 кГц, вода или ацетон, мишень 2 мм/с; 100 мкДж, 5 кГц — насыщение 15 мин, ~100 мкг/мл; ζ-потенциал −30 мВ при пороге 20 мВ (с. 2). Размер: 10→100 мкДж даёт 25→40 нм в ацетоне, в воде ~30 нм; пик ~700 нм (с. 2). Фрагментация: в воде окисление, в ацетоне до 4 нм (FWHM <3 нм), сдвиг 700→640 нм; экстинкция 18→6 л·г⁻¹·см⁻¹ (с. 3). 9: [источник] Дословные цитаты для сверки:
10: 
11: - «for 100 μJ pulse energy and 5 kHz repetition rate saturation time was 15 min» (с. 2)
12: - «the increase of pulse energy from 10 to 100 μJ led to the increase of NPs mean diameter from 25 to 40 nm» (с. 2)
13: - «we observed a drastic decrease in the size of final TiN NPs down to 4 nm» (с. 3)
14: 
15: 
16: # L1 — часть 02 (PDF с. 4–7)
17: 
18: [порождено] В 2D-культурах TiN до 10 мкг/мл нетоксичен для U87–MG: выживаемость >90% (91±3%); у HMEC–1 она снижена до 71±3% уже с 0,5 мкг/мл (с. 4). В сфероидах U87–MG после 13 суток воздействия морфология не менялась при ≤1 мкг/мл; при ≥5 мкг/мл площадь уменьшалась на 6±5%, 22±8% и 37±8% для 5, 10 и 15 мкг/мл, выживаемость составляла 93±9%, 77±8% и 74±11% (с. 6). НЧ обнаруживались кластерами в эндосомах, но не в лизосомах и ядрах (с. 6). 27: # L1 — часть 03 (с. 8–11 PDF)
28: 
29: [порождено] Часть охватывает с. 8–11 PDF. Синтез: абляция массивной мишени TiN фемтосекундным лазером (Yb:KGW, 1025 нм, 1–100 кГц, пучок 2,3 мм, линза 75 мм) в 7 мл воды (18,2 МОм·см при 25 °C) или ацетона; слой жидкости 10 мм, мишень движется 2 мм/с (с. 8). Фрагментация — облучение коллоида тем же лазером без мишени, фокус на 1 см ниже поверхности, магнитная мешалка; иногда кислород удаляли барботированием Ar (с. 8). Методы: HR-TEM 300 кВ, ζ-потенциал, UV-VIS, ICP-MS (с. 9). Цитотоксичность: HMEC-1 и U87-MG в 2D (0,025–10 мкг/мл, 72 ч) и сфероиды U87-MG (0,1–15 мкг/мл, 13 сут); фототермия: CW 670 нм, 4,4 Вт/см² (310 мВт, 3 мм), 1–15 мин (с. 9). 1: www.nature.com/scientificreports/
2: 2Scientific  RepoRts  |          (2019) 9:1194  | https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-018-37519-1
3: of generating red-shifted plasmonic feature16–21 with a high photothermal conversion efficiency21. Having good 
4: chemical stability and biocompatibility, TiN instruments have been successfully used in biological systems as 
5: surgical and food-related tools, as well as implants22, while well-established surface chemistry of TiN structures 
6: renders possible its easy functionalization by standard protocols23. However, fabrication routes for the synthesis of 
7: TiN NPs are not always compatible with projected biomedical applications. Indeed, chemical synthesis routes24,25 
8: are rather complicated in terms of a number of preparation steps and employ hazardous products, which can 
9: cause residual contamination of NPs and related toxicity issues. On the other hand, nanocrystals prepared by 
10: dry fabrication methods, including direct nitridation of TiO
11: 2 powders26, plasma assisted processing27–29 and laser 
12: ablation in nitrogen atmosphere 17, normally cannot be dispersed and stabilized in aqueous solutions without 
13: applying similar wet chemistry steps.
14: Here, we demonstrate a simple and cost efficient method for the production of stable solutions of bare (ligand –  
15: free) TiN NPs by methods of femtosecond (fs) laser ablation and fragmentation in water and organic (acetone) 
16: solutions. By performing a series of biological tests using 2D cultures and 3D spheroids, we evidence high safety 
17: and excellent cell uptake of laser-synthesized TiN NPs, as well as show efficient therapy effect on cancer cells using 
18: TiN NPs as sensitizers of photothermal treatment at the plasmonic absorption band (650–800 nm).
19: Results and Discussion
20: synthesis and characterization of t iN nanoparticles.  For the synthesis of TiN NPs we adapted 
21: methods of ultra-short laser ablation and fragmentation in liquid ambience, which were earlier used for the 
22: preparation of bare Au and Ag NPs
23: 30–36. In the first “ablation” approach30–32, radiation from a femtosecond laser 
24: (Yb:KGW , 1025 nm, 1–100 kHz) was focused onto a TiN target placed on the bottom of a glass vessel filled with 
25: deionized water or acetone in order to initiate ablation of material, as shown in Fig.  1a (see details in Methods 
26: section). The target was continuously moved at a speed of 2 mm s− 1 during the ablation step to avoid ablation 
27: from the same point.
28: We observed a blue coloration of solution within a few minutes of the ablation process, indicating the for -
29: mation of TiN NPs. Concentration of NPs increased linearly at the beginning of the process and then came to 
30: a saturation after some time. Saturation concentration and time until saturation depended on pulse energy. In 
31: particular, for 100 μJ pulse energy and 5 kHz repetition rate saturation time was 15 min and the saturation con-
32: centration was about 100 μg mL
33: − 1. TiN colloids synthesized by laser ablation both in water and acetone were very 
34: stable with almost no traces of aggregation or precipitation during their storage at ambient conditions for several 
35: months. Such a high stability of colloidal solutions was due to an electrostatic stabilization owing to strong charg-
36: ing of NPs surface similar to how it happens for other materials
37: 33. Indeed, according to our ζ–potential measure-
38: ments, the surface potential of TiN NPs was − 30 mV , which is higher than the stability threshold (20 mV)37 for 
39: colloidal solutions.
40: A typical HR-TEM image of a TiN nanoparticle synthesized by pulsed laser ablation in water is shown in 
41: Fig. 2a. One can see that the nanoparticle had a spherical shape and exhibited a polycrystalline structure, while 
42: the size of single-crystal grains was about 1–3 nm. Interestingly, TiN NPs could have a hollow structure con-
43: taining one or several cavities, as follows from the presence of light areas inside NPs on TEM images (Fig.  2e). 
44: When synthesized in acetone, only 5–10% of NPs contained such hollow cavities, while for the synthesis in water 
45: ambient the relevant parameter could reach 60%. Moreover, most of hollow NPs had only one cavity under ace-
46: tone conditions, while under water conditions they could contain several cavities. As another observation, when 
47: ablated in acetone, all synthesized TiN NPs were spherical and crystalline, while the ablation in water ambient 
48: was accompanied by the production of a certain amount of nanostructured amorphous flakes. Based on our pre-
49: vious experience, the formation of such amorphous non-spherical flakes during laser ablation in water is typical 
50: for easily oxidizing materials (Ti, Fe, Co, etc.). Nevertheless, SAED measurements showed that spherical NPs 
51: prepared under water and acetone conditions present stoichiometric TiN. An example of SAED pattern is shown 
52: in Fig. 2b. Results of analysis of this pattern are summarized in Table 1. Rings 3, 4 and 6–11 correspond to first 
53: 8 diffraction rings of TiN FCC lattice, as follows from the comparison of their positions with data for bulk TiN, 
54: taken from JCPDS database (JCPDS 38–1420). Measured lattice constant 4.272 Å ± 0.114 Å is in accordance with 
55: tabulated lattice constant 4.24 Å of bulk TiN. Rings 1 and 5, which cannot be attributed to rock salt structure of 
56: TiN, should belong to titanium oxide fraction of synthesized NPs. In particular, position of ring 1 is close to that 
57: of (012) plane of Ti
58: 2O3 (JCPDS 43-1033), the position of ring 5 is close to (105) plane of anatase TiO2 and (211) 
59: plane of rutile TiO2 (JCPDS 21-1272 and 21-1276). Thus, SAED data clearly indicated formation of crystalline 
60: TiN NPs with lattice structure similar to that of bulk TiN with some fraction of titanium oxide. Presence of 
61: titanium oxide is in accordance with previous results on the synthesis of TiN NPs by alternative methods
62: 20,23,25.
63: Statistical analysis of TEM images demonstrated lognormal size distribution of synthesized TiN NPs as shown 
64: in Fig. 2c. When ablated in acetone, the mean size of NPs depended on laser pulse energy as shown in Fig. 3. In 
65: particular, the increase of pulse energy from 10 to 100 μJ led to the increase of NPs mean diameter from 25 to 
66: 40 nm under relatively broad size dispersion (25–40 nm FWHM). Such a pulse energy dependence for the mean 
67: size of TiN NPs is in agreement with our previous data on fs laser ablation of Au in deionized water30,31. For abla-
68: tion in water, the dependence of NPs size on pulse energy was not significant and the mean size of synthesized 
69: TiN NPs was always around 30 nm under the size dispersion of 40 nm FWHM. It is important that TiN NPs pre-
70: pared both in acetone and deionized water exhibited strong peaks around 700 nm in extinction spectra associated 
71: with the excitation of surface plasmons over the NPs (solid black and red lines in Fig. 4, respectively). Here, we 
72: did not observe any remarkable variations of the peak position for NPs having mean size between 25 and 40 nm. 
73: It should be noted that TiN NPs prepared in acetone could be easily transferred to aqueous solutions via a simple 
74: centrifugation step.
75: To further reduce the mean size and narrow down size dispersion, we employed the technique of femtosecond 
76: laser fragmentation, which was developed in our earlier works to minimize the size dispersion of bare Au NPs
77: 34–36.

3: Similar results were obtained with 3D cell cultures in spheroids form, which are more representative of 
4: tumors-related objects as their cell morphology and phenotype are similar to those found in the original tissue 
5: architecture (tumors). Such spheroids are typically composed of clusters of cells with a dense tissue and a com-
6: plex cellular organization due to absence of a culture plastic substrate. In addition, they have diffusional limits 
7: to transport of drugs, nutrients and other factors similar to in vivo tissues
8: 40,41. Safety of TiN NPs was assessed on 
9: U87–MG cells grown as spheroids and continuously exposed to different concentrations of TiN NPs for 13 days. 
10: Concentrations of 1 μg mL
11: − 1 and lower caused no evident morphological alterations of spheroids as compared 
12: to controls (Fig. 6a). However, after two weeks of exposure spheroids treated with doses of TiN NPs higher than 
13: 5 μg mL− 1 exhibited irregular shapes and smaller cross-sectional areas as compared to controls. Moreover, after 
14: two weeks of continuous exposure, a loss of cell cohesion and the presence of debris were also visible for TiN NPs
